source_policy: Primary issuer documents and original research-provider publication. Secondary search results were discovery leads only. No numeric Mercury share estimate is adopted because an accessible original current table was not located.

sources.facts: Projects server-CPU shipments +31% in2026 and >40% in2027. Chart labels inner2026(E), outer2027(F): Intel50/42, AMD27/28, NVIDIA12/12, AWS4/5, Google3/6, Others4/7 percent. Context is shipments, not revenue; chart title itself says market shares. Captive cloud CPUs are included.
sources.interpretation: Intel can grow units while losing share. Figures are rounded forecasts and do not establish actual2026 or2027 share.

sources.facts: Management describes server-CPU TAM potentially rising from about$40B to more than$200B over five years, primarily agentic workloads. It forecasts industry CPU units >30% in2026 and2027.
sources.scope: The five-year endpoint is roughly2031, not expressly FY2030. Current$40B is not a dated auditedFY2026 market total. Merchant versus captive dollar valuation is not disclosed.
sources.interpretation: Supports a large expanding CPU pool; does not establish exact2030 sales, an Intel share, or terminal growth.

sources.facts: DCAI revenue is$7.318B Q3 and$18.632B YTD; rounded Other DCAI is$1.4B/$3.3B. Residual CPU proxies are$5.918B/$15.332B. Q3 server units +10%, ASP+54%; YTD units+4%, ASP+44%; richer product mix is the main ASP driver.
sources.scope: Residuals inherit rounded Other values; units and ASP are YoY for respective reported periods. CPU residual excludes purpose-built Other DCAI and is not totalDCAI.

sources.facts: CPU revenue grew >50%YoY. Management raised server-CPU TAM to >$120B by2030, >35%annual growth, and discussed general-purpose, accelerator head-node and agentic CPU workloads. It expressed an ambition above50%market share.
sources.scope: This is an older forecast superseded by Q2. Architecture competition is discussed, but captive dollar-accounting methodology is not specified. AMD ambition is not an independent prediction of realizedshare.

sources.facts: Server-CPU market forecast is approximately$220B in2030 (>50%annual growth), distinct from$1.4T accelerators. Agentic sandboxes are forecast to become the largestCPU category. ActualQ2 EPYC revenue grew >70%YoY; units andASP both grew double digits, with units contributing more. Management forecast CPU revenue >80%H22026 and>70%FY2027.
sources.scope: No absolute CPU-only revenue total or exact unit/ASP growth pair is disclosed here. Captive versus merchant dollar accounting remains unclear.

sources.facts: DataCenter$8.546B and97%growth include EPYC CPUs andInstinct GPUs. Results support strong demand but cannot be used asCPU-only revenue orCPU market share.

baseline_policy.preferred_observation: Use Intel reported YTD CPU residual and separately labeled FY2026E model anchors, plus TrendForce estimated shipment shares. There is no verified, consistently defined globalCPU-dollar-share baseline in these sources.
baseline_policy.warning: 54.64% is an illustrative quotient of modelFY2026E and management approximatecurrentTAM; never label it observed Intel globalrevenue share. Nor convert TrendForce50%shipment share into50%revenue share.
